examples.en: The electric train slowly pulls into the station.

examples.ko: 출근 시간에는 전동차 안이 너무 붐벼요.
examples.en: The train is far too crowded during rush hour.
I missed the last train, so I took a taxi.
The new trains have much more comfortable seats.
The train doors are closing, so be careful.
The children watched the trains pass by outside the window.

explain: 일상에서는 보통 '지하철'이나 '전철'이라고 해요. '전동차'는 열차 자체를 가리킬 때나 안내 방송, 뉴스에서 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: In daily speech people usually say 지하철 or 전철. 전동차 refers to the train itself and is heard more often in station announcements and the news.

examples.en: The paper folds neatly in half.

examples.ko: 우산이 접히지 않아서 가방에 못 넣었어요.
examples.en: The umbrella wouldn't fold, so I couldn't put it in my bag.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 접혀서 차에 쉽게 실을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This chair folds up, so it's easy to load into a car.
I bought a desk whose legs fold.
The wind made the umbrella suddenly fold shut.

examples.ko: 이 지도는 아주 작게 접힐 거예요.
examples.en: This map will fold up very small.

explain: '접다'는 내가 접는 것이고 '접히다'는 저절로, 또는 힘을 받아서 접어지는 거예요. 그래서 '종이를 접다'가 '종이가 접히다'가 되면서 조사가 '를'에서 '가'로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: 접다 is when someone folds something; 접히다 is when it gets folded by itself or by force. So the particle changes from 를 to 가: '종이를 접다' becomes '종이가 접히다'.

examples.ko: 조교수님이 이번 학기 수업을 맡게 되셨어요.
examples.en: The assistant professor will teach this semester's class.
I became an assistant professor at a university this year.

examples.ko: 김 조교수는 연구실에서 논문을 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: Assistant Professor Kim is writing a paper in the lab.
You need a doctorate to become an assistant professor.
The students asked the assistant professor a lot of questions.
That assistant professor is very popular with students.

explain: 대학교 교수 직급은 보통 조교수, 부교수, 교수 순서로 올라가요. 직접 부를 때는 '조교수님'보다 그냥 '교수님'이라고 하는 경우가 훨씬 많아요. '조교'는 수업을 돕는 사람이라 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: University ranks usually go 조교수, 부교수, 교수. When addressing someone directly, people far more often just say 교수님. Note that 조교 is a teaching assistant, which is a different thing.

examples.en: Middle-distance running is hard but fun.

examples.ko: 그 선수가 중거리 슛으로 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: That player scored with a long-range shot.

examples.ko: 중거리 비행은 보통 서너 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: A medium-haul flight usually takes three or four hours.

examples.ko: 저는 단거리보다 중거리를 더 잘 뛰어요.
examples.en: I run middle distances better than sprints.

examples.ko: 이 차는 중거리 여행에 딱 맞아요.
examples.en: This car is just right for mid-range trips.

examples.ko: 우리 학교에서 중거리 달리기 대회가 열려요.
examples.en: A middle-distance running race is being held at our school.

explain: '단거리', '중거리', '장거리'로 나눠서 달리기, 수영, 비행 같은 데 써요. 일상에서 멀지도 가깝지도 않은 거리를 말할 때는 보통 '적당한 거리'라고 해요.
explain_en: Distances are split into 단거리, 중거리 and 장거리 for running, swimming and flights. In everyday talk about a not-near-not-far distance, people usually say 적당한 거리 instead.

examples.en: Try wringing out the wet towel tightly.
I squeezed a lemon into the water.

examples.ko: 아무리 머리를 쥐어짜도 생각이 안 나요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I rack my brain, I can't remember.
If you wring out the laundry, a lot of water comes out.
The toothpaste was almost gone, so I squeezed out every last bit.
It hurt as if my heart were being wrung.

explain: '짜다'보다 손에 힘을 더 줘서 꽉 쥐고 누르는 느낌이에요. 수건이나 레몬 같은 물건에도 쓰고, '머리를 쥐어짜다'처럼 애써서 생각을 짜낼 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 머리를 쥐어짜서 겨우 아이디어를 하나 냈어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방법이 안 떠오를 때 애써서 열심히 생각하는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes thinking very hard when no idea comes easily.

explain_en: Compared with 짜다, it feels like gripping and pressing harder with your hand. It is used for towels and lemons, and also for forcing out ideas, as in '머리를 쥐어짜다'.

examples.ko: 이 과자에는 첨가물이 거의 안 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This snack has almost no additives in it.

examples.ko: 식품 첨가물은 포장지 뒤에 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: Food additives are listed on the back of the package.
I bought juice with no additives.

examples.ko: 아이에게 첨가물 많은 음식을 주고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to give my child food full of additives.

examples.ko: 화학 첨가물을 줄이는 회사가 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More companies are cutting back on chemical additives.
The taste turned a bit strange because of the additives.

explain: '재료'는 음식의 기본이 되는 것이고, '첨가물'은 맛이나 색, 보관을 위해 따로 더한 것이에요. 포장지에서 '식품 첨가물', '무첨가'라는 말을 자주 봐요.
explain_en: 재료 is what a dish is basically made of, while 첨가물 is something added separately for taste, color or storage. You often see 식품 첨가물 and 무첨가 on packaging.

examples.en: I saw a bronze sword at the museum.
People farmed in the Bronze Age.

examples.ko: 이 청동기는 삼천 년 전에 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: This bronze piece was made three thousand years ago.
A bronze artifact was found underground.
We learned about the Bronze Age in history class.
The mirror made of bronze is amazing.

explain: '청동기 시대'라는 역사 용어로 가장 많이 써요. 한국사 수업에서는 '구석기', '신석기', '청동기', '철기' 순서로 배워요.
explain_en: It is used most often in the history term 청동기 시대 (Bronze Age). In Korean history class you learn the order 구석기, 신석기, 청동기, 철기.

examples.en: A friend sang a congratulatory song at the wedding.
Who is going to sing the celebration song?

examples.ko: 축가 연습을 매일 저녁에 하고 있어요.
examples.en: I practice the celebration song every evening.
Which song should we choose for the celebration?
The song lifted the whole mood.
The song at my sibling's wedding was so moving.

explain: 결혼식에서 가장 많이 들어요. 보통 친구나 가수가 신랑 신부를 위해 부르고 '축가를 부르다'로 같이 써요. 생일에 부르는 노래는 '축가'보다 '생일 노래'라고 해요.
explain_en: You hear it mostly at weddings, where a friend or singer performs for the couple. It pairs with 부르다: '축가를 부르다'. For a birthday, people say 생일 노래 rather than 축가.

examples.en: The tallest kid in our class is good at basketball.
I read a book called Daddy-Long-Legs.
I was surprised that my younger sibling became so tall.
His friends call him Beanpole.

examples.ko: 키다리 형이 높은 선반의 상자를 내려 줬어요.
examples.en: The tall guy took down the box from the high shelf for me.
Tall people can easily bump their heads on doors.

explain: '키 큰 사람'은 평범한 말이고 '키다리'는 친근하게 놀리는 듯한 느낌이 있어요. '키다리 아저씨'는 유명한 책 제목이에요. 키 작은 사람을 놀리는 '땅꼬마'는 실례가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: 키 큰 사람 is the neutral phrase, while 키다리 has a friendly, teasing tone. '키다리 아저씨' is the Korean title of Daddy-Long-Legs. Its opposite 땅꼬마 can be rude.

examples.en: The ball hit the wall and bounced back.
I flicked the marble with my finger.
If you pluck a guitar string, it makes a sound.
The stone skipped across the water.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일부러 튕기는 것 같아요.
examples.en: She seems to be playing hard to get on purpose.
Raindrops bounced off the umbrella and wet my clothes.

explain: '튀다'와 비슷하지만 '튕기다'는 손가락이나 줄을 세게 쳐서 퉁 하고 움직이게 할 때도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 관심 있으면서도 일부러 쉽게 받아 주지 않는 모습을 말해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 관심이 있어도 일부러 바로 받아 주지 않는 모습을 말하는 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Colloquial: refusing or delaying on purpose despite being interested.

explain_en: Similar to 튀다, but 튕기다 also covers flicking a finger or plucking a string. Said of a person, it means acting hard to get on purpose even though they are interested.

examples.en: Morning dew is clinging to the blades of grass.
I plucked a blade of grass and held it in my mouth.
The blades of grass sway gently in the wind.
The child made a small boat out of a leaf of grass.
The tip of the grass was sharp and cut my hand.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 풀잎 냄새가 진하게 났어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, there was a strong smell of grass.

explain: '풀'은 식물 전체이고 '풀잎'은 그 풀의 잎 한 장이에요. 이슬이나 바람 장면에서 시처럼 자주 나와요. 나무의 잎은 '나뭇잎'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 풀 is the plant as a whole, while 풀잎 is a single leaf of it. It shows up often in poetic scenes with dew or wind. A tree's leaf is 나뭇잎.

examples.ko: 새 공항 후보지가 세 곳으로 정해졌어요.
examples.en: Three candidate sites were chosen for the new airport.
Our city was also listed as a candidate site for the Olympics.

examples.ko: 회사가 새 공장 후보지를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is looking for candidate sites for a new factory.

examples.ko: 이 섬은 영화 촬영 후보지로 거론돼요.
examples.en: This island is mentioned as a possible filming location.
I visited both candidate sites and compared them.
The candidate sites will be announced next week.

explain: '후보'는 사람과 물건에 두루 쓰지만 '후보지'는 어디에 지을지, 어디서 열지 아직 정해지기 전의 장소에만 써요. 뉴스에서 '건설 후보지', '개최 후보지'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 후보 works for people and things, but 후보지 is only for places not yet decided on, such as where to build or hold something. You see 건설 후보지 and 개최 후보지 in the news.

examples.en: The baby is eating happily, yum-yum.
Yum-yum, this cake is really delicious!
The puppy is munching on its treat.

examples.ko: 우리 딸은 냠냠 소리를 내면서 밥을 먹어요.
examples.en: My daughter makes yum-yum sounds while eating.
After eating it all up, I'm full.

examples.ko: 자, 이제 우리 같이 냠냠 해 볼까요?
examples.en: Now, shall we dig in together?

explain: 아이에게 '냠냠 먹자'처럼 말하거나 동화, 아기 말투에서 써요. 어른끼리 진지한 자리에서는 잘 안 써요. '쩝쩝'은 입 소리가 시끄럽다는 느낌이라 칭찬이 아니에요.
explain_en: It is used when talking to children ('냠냠 먹자'), in picture books and baby talk, but rarely between adults in a serious setting. 쩝쩝 is a smacking noise and is not a compliment.

examples.en: I made broth with anchovies and kelp.
Kelp gets soft when you soak it in water.
I eat fried kelp chips as a snack.
I bought dried kelp at the market.
The broth is clean-tasting because kelp went into it.

examples.ko: 삶은 다시마에 밥과 고기를 싸 먹었어요.
examples.en: I wrapped rice and meat in boiled kelp and ate it.

explain: 미역과 비슷하지만 다시마는 더 두껍고 넓어서 주로 국물을 낼 때 써요. 멸치와 함께 넣어 육수를 내는 게 가장 흔해요.
explain_en: It looks like 미역 but 다시마 is thicker and wider, and it is mainly used to make broth. Boiling it together with anchovies for 육수 is the most common use.

examples.en: Thick socks are nice in winter.
My younger sibling has full lips, so they look cute.
This notebook has nicely thick paper.
I grilled thickly sliced meat.
The blanket is thick, so it will be warm.
The cardigan was thick but not heavy.

explain: '두껍다'는 그냥 두께가 있다는 뜻이고, '도톰하다'는 적당히 두꺼워서 따뜻하거나 보기 좋다는 느낌이 있어요. 옷, 입술, 고기, 종이에 자주 써요. 너무 두꺼울 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: 두껍다 just says something has thickness, while 도톰하다 suggests it is moderately thick in a nice or cozy way. It is common for clothes, lips, meat and paper, but not for something excessively thick.

examples.en: It's payday, so my wallet is full.
I slept under a thick, well-stuffed cotton quilt.
I received a generous bonus.
Dad's pocket was always full of allowance money.
I feel good looking at my fattened bank account.
The winter jacket is thickly padded, so it's warm to wear.

explain: 돈이 넉넉할 때 '지갑이 두둑하다', '용돈을 두둑이 주다'처럼 써요. 옷이나 이불이 두껍고 속이 꽉 찬 것에도 쓰지만 요즘 대화에서는 돈 이야기에서 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 주머니가 아니라 돈이 넉넉하다는 뜻으로 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not about an actual pocket; it means one has plenty of money.

explain_en: It is used for plenty of money: '지갑이 두둑하다', '용돈을 두둑이 주다'. It also fits thick, well-padded clothes and quilts, but these days it comes up mostly in talk about money.

en: get drawn into; get caught up in

examples.en: I don't want to get dragged into my friends' fight.
My sleeve almost got caught in the machine.
I had a hard time after getting caught up in that incident.
I rescued a person being swept into the waves.
Be careful not to get mixed up in bad things.
The child struggled after being caught up in a rumor.

explain: '휘말리다'와 거의 같게 써요. 내가 원하지 않았는데 싸움, 사고, 소문 같은 나쁜 일에 끌려 들어갈 때 써요. 좋은 일에는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used almost like 휘말리다. It describes being pulled into trouble such as a fight, an accident or a rumor when you didn't want to be. It is not used for good things.

examples.en: Every autumn we go see the fall leaves.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 매해 새 제품을 내놓아요.
examples.en: That company releases a new product every year.
Every year on my birthday I have a meal with my family.
It rains a lot around this time every year.
The festival is held every year, so I look forward to it.
I save a little bit every year.

explain: '매년'과 같은 뜻이지만 '매해'는 조금 더 부드럽고 글이나 이야기 느낌이 있어요. 말할 때는 '해마다'나 '매년'이 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Same meaning as 매년, but 매해 sounds softer and a bit more written or storylike. In speech, 해마다 and 매년 come up more often.

examples.ko: 배가 너무 아파서 맹장 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: My stomach hurt so much that I had an appendix check.
I had an appendix operation and stayed a week in the hospital.
It's dangerous if the appendix bursts.
My younger sibling got appendicitis.

examples.ko: 오른쪽 아랫배가 아프면 맹장일 수 있어요.
examples.en: If your lower right belly hurts, it could be the appendix.
Where in the body is the appendix?

explain: 병원에서는 '충수'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '맹장'이라고 해요. 염증이 생긴 병은 보통 '맹장염'이라고 하고, 수술은 '맹장 수술'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: In medical settings it can be called 충수, but in daily life people say 맹장. The inflamed condition is usually 맹장염, and the operation is called 맹장 수술.

examples.en: Noodles made from buckwheat are refreshing.
A buckwheat pillow is easy on the neck.
I ate buckwheat crepes in Gangwon Province.
The buckwheat flower field bloomed white.

examples.ko: 메밀은 쌀이나 밀보다 구수한 맛이 나요.
examples.en: Buckwheat has a nuttier flavor than rice or wheat.
In summer I often eat buckwheat noodles.

explain: 음식으로는 '메밀국수', '메밀묵', '메밀 전병'처럼 이어서 많이 써요. '모밀'이라고 하는 사람도 있지만 표준어는 '메밀'이에요.
explain_en: In food it is often part of compounds such as 메밀국수, 메밀묵 and 메밀 전병. Some people say 모밀, but the standard form is 메밀.

examples.en: I ordered clam noodle soup.
You have to let clams purge, so the sand comes out.
I bought fresh clams at the market.
Adding clams to soybean stew makes it refreshing.

examples.ko: 바지락이 입을 벌리면 다 익은 거예요.
examples.en: When the clams open their shells, they're done.
I dug up clams at the beach.

explain: 조개 중에서도 칼국수나 된장찌개 같은 국물 요리에 가장 흔하게 들어가요. 요리 전에 소금물에 담가 모래를 빼는 일을 '해감'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the clam most commonly put into broths such as 칼국수 and 된장찌개. Soaking clams in salt water to remove sand before cooking is called 해감.

examples.en: The puppy has fleas on its body.
Fleas jump very high.
I got bitten by fleas and my legs itch.
I applied medicine to get rid of the cat's fleas.

examples.ko: 벼룩이 생기지 않게 자주 빗질해 줘요.
examples.en: I brush it often so fleas don't appear.
I bought a used book at the flea market.

explain: 작은 곤충이라 보통 반려동물 이야기에서 나와요. '벼룩시장'은 영어의 flea market을 옮긴 말로, 중고 물건을 사고파는 곳이에요.

phrases.example: 그 적은 월급까지 떼어 가다니, 벼룩의 간을 빼 먹는 일이에요.
phrases.en: take from someone who has almost nothing
phrases.nuance_ko: 가진 것이 거의 없는 사람의 것까지 빼앗는 야박한 행동을 나무랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone who takes even from those with almost nothing.
phrases.en_equiv: take from the poorest of the poor

explain_en: It is a tiny insect and mostly comes up in talk about pets. 벼룩시장 is the Korean version of 'flea market', a place to buy and sell second-hand goods.

examples.en: The market has all sorts of things.
I've met every kind of person.

examples.ko: 별별 생각이 다 들어서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: All kinds of thoughts came to me, so I couldn't sleep.
All sorts of stories get posted on the internet.

examples.ko: 오늘은 별별 일이 다 생긴 하루였어요.
examples.en: Today was a day when all sorts of things happened.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 별별 음식을 다 팔아요.
examples.en: That shop sells every kind of food.

explain: '별별' 뒤에는 '사람', '일', '생각' 같은 말이 와서 '별별 사람', '별별 일'처럼 써요. 보통 '다'와 함께 '별별 게 다 있다'라고 하면서 놀라거나 어이없어하는 느낌을 담아요.
explain_en: It is followed by a noun like 사람, 일 or 생각, as in '별별 사람', '별별 일'. It often pairs with 다, as in '별별 게 다 있다', carrying a sense of surprise or disbelief.

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 수호신을 모신 나무가 있어요.
examples.en: At the village entrance is a tree that enshrines the guardian spirit.

examples.ko: 이 부적은 나를 지켜 주는 수호신 같아요.
examples.en: This charm feels like a guardian that protects me.
In that game I became the guardian.
Grandma said the jangseung is the village's guardian spirit.
Our team's guardian angel is the goalkeeper.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 이 곰 인형이 제 수호신이었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, this teddy bear was my protector.

explain: 원래는 마을이나 집을 지켜 준다고 믿는 신이지만, 지금은 비유로 더 자주 써요. 중요한 순간마다 나를 지켜 주는 사람이나 물건을 '수호신'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: Originally a god believed to protect a village or home, but today it is more often used figuratively. A person or object that protects you at key moments is called a 수호신.

examples.en: I can see the grains of rice one by one.
Pomegranate seeds are tasty even if you chew them whole.
I put the corn kernels on a plate.

examples.ko: 이 비누는 작은 알갱이로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This soap is made of tiny granules.

examples.ko: 소금 알갱이가 굵어서 잘 녹지 않아요.
examples.en: The salt grains are coarse, so they don't dissolve easily.
Grains of sand got inside my shoe.

explain: 쌀, 소금, 모래, 곡식처럼 가루보다는 크고 덩어리보다는 작은 낱개에 잘 어울려요. 세는 말은 '쌀 한 알'처럼 '알'을 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It suits things like rice, salt, sand and grain: bigger than powder, smaller than lumps. The counter 알 is often used, as in '쌀 한 알'.

examples.en: Grandma keeps kimchi in an earthenware jar.
An onggi jar is a vessel that breathes.
I bought a small earthenware pot at the market.
Bowls made of earthenware are heavy but sturdy.

examples.ko: 옹기 마을에서 직접 항아리를 빚어 봤어요.
examples.en: I shaped a jar myself in the pottery village.
Earthenware jars are lined up on the jangdokdae.

explain: 된장, 간장, 김치를 담는 갈색 항아리가 대표적이에요. '도자기'는 높은 온도에서 구운 매끈한 그릇이고, '옹기'는 숨구멍이 있어서 발효 음식을 두기에 좋다고 해요.
explain_en: The typical example is the brown jar for 된장, 간장 and 김치. 도자기 is smooth, high-fired ware, whereas 옹기 is porous and said to be good for fermented food.

examples.en: I ruined the presentation and got blamed by my teammates.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 무례한 말 때문에 크게 욕먹었어요.
examples.en: That singer was heavily criticized for rude remarks.
I spoke honestly, ready to be criticized.
Sometimes you get criticized even when you do well.

examples.ko: 괜히 나만 욕먹는 것 같아서 억울해요.
examples.en: It feels unfair, as if only I am getting blamed.

examples.ko: 실수했다고 너무 욕먹으면 기분이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: If you get blamed too much for a mistake, it feels bad.

explain: '야단맞다'는 주로 윗사람에게 혼나는 것이고, '욕먹다'는 사람들에게 나쁜 말이나 비난을 듣는 거예요. 인터넷이나 뉴스에서 많이 쓰고 '욕을 먹다'로 띄어 써도 같아요.
explain_en: 야단맞다 is mostly being told off by someone above you, while 욕먹다 is hearing bad words or criticism from people in general. It is common online and in the news, and '욕을 먹다' is the same thing.

examples.en: It was raining, so I went out in a raincoat.
The yellow raincoat suits the child well.
I carry a raincoat in my bag.

examples.ko: 우산 대신 우비를 입으면 손이 자유로워요.
examples.en: If you wear a raincoat instead of using an umbrella, your hands are free.
Pack a raincoat too when you go on a picnic.

examples.ko: 그 우비는 바람이 불어도 안 젖어요.
examples.en: That raincoat doesn't get wet even in the wind.

explain: '우비'와 '비옷'은 거의 같은 말인데, 아이들 이야기에서는 '우비'가 더 자주 나와요. 우산 대신 입으면 두 손을 쓸 수 있어서 어린이나 자전거 탈 때 많이 입어요. 우산은 '쓰다', 우비는 '입다'로 동사가 달라요.
explain_en: '우비' and '비옷' are nearly the same word, but '우비' comes up more often when talking about children. It frees both hands, so kids and cyclists wear it a lot. The verbs differ: you 쓰다 an umbrella, but 입다 a raincoat.

examples.en: I packed jerky when I went hiking.
Jerky is salty, so it's good as a snack.
Beef jerky tends to be expensive.
I chewed the jerky for a long time.
I bought a bag of jerky at the convenience store.
The jerky was so hard that it was difficult to eat.

explain: 소고기로 만든 것을 가장 먼저 떠올리지만 돼지고기나 닭고기로 만든 것도 있어요. 짭짤해서 등산이나 여행 간식으로 인기가 있어요.
explain_en: People think of beef first, but there is also pork and chicken jerky. It is salty and popular as a snack for hiking or trips.

examples.en: My pitch keeps going off when I sing.
I practice matching the pitch every day.

examples.ko: 기타 음정이 맞지 않으면 소리가 이상해요.
examples.en: If the guitar isn't in tune, it sounds odd.

examples.ko: 음정과 박자를 둘 다 지키기가 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to keep both pitch and rhythm.
In a choir, the pitches have to match each other.

examples.ko: 높은 음정은 목에 힘이 많이 들어가요.
examples.en: High pitches take a lot of effort in the throat.

explain: 노래에서 '음정'은 소리의 높낮이가 맞는지를, '박자'는 시간에 맞게 부르는지를 가리켜요. '음정이 틀리다', '음정이 안 맞다', '음정을 맞추다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In singing, 음정 is whether the pitch is right, and 박자 is whether it is on time. Typical phrases are '음정이 틀리다', '음정이 안 맞다' and '음정을 맞추다'.

examples.en: There are four members in our group.
I made the presentation materials with my group members.

examples.ko: 조원 중에 한 명이 아파서 결석했어요.
examples.en: One of the group members was sick and absent.
The group members gathered and divided up the roles.
A new member joined and brightened the mood.

examples.ko: 저희 조원은 모두 열심히 해서 고마워요.
examples.en: I'm grateful that everyone in our group worked hard.

explain: 학교 수업이나 모임에서 여럿이 한 '조'로 묶일 때 그 안의 사람이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '팀원'도 쓰는데 학교에서는 '조원', 회사나 운동에서는 '팀원'이 더 자연스러워요. 숫자 뒤의 '조 원'(trillion won)과는 달라요.
explain_en: It is a person in a 조 (group) formed in class or a gathering. 팀원 is similar, but 조원 sounds natural at school and 팀원 at work or in sports. It is unrelated to '조 원' (trillion won) after a number.

examples.en: Please check whether this painting is genuine.
That bag is authentic, so it's expensive.
The appraiser told the genuine one from the fake.
At the museum, the originals are inside glass.
The watch I bought online wasn't genuine.
I want the genuine one, but it's too expensive.

explain: '진품'의 반대는 '가짜', 모조품은 '모조품', 위조된 그림이나 글씨는 '위작'이에요. 비슷한 '정품'은 회사가 공식으로 판 제품이고, '진품'은 진짜 작품이나 골동품 쪽에 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: The opposite of 진품 is 가짜; imitations are 모조품, and forged paintings or calligraphy are 위작. 정품 means an officially sold product, while 진품 fits real artworks and antiques better.

examples.en: The waste disposal site is outside the city.
They clean the water at the sewage treatment plant.

examples.ko: 처리장 근처에는 냄새가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: There can be a smell near the treatment plant.
Residents opposed the construction of a new facility.
We moved the waste to the disposal site.

examples.ko: 우리 동네에는 처리장이 두 곳 있어요.
examples.en: There are two treatment plants in my neighborhood.

explain: '쓰레기 처리장', '폐기물 처리장', '하수 처리장'처럼 앞에 무엇을 처리하는지 붙여서 써요. 혼자 쓰이는 경우는 드물어요. '처리 시설'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It is usually preceded by what is being processed: 쓰레기 처리장, 폐기물 처리장, 하수 처리장. It is rarely used alone. 처리 시설 is used in a similar way.

examples.en: A memorial ceremony was held at school yesterday.
Many people attended the memorial ceremony.
The memorial ceremony was held quietly and solemnly.
My friends laid flowers at the memorial ceremony.
We prepared a memorial service in honor of that person.

examples.ko: 추모식이 끝난 뒤에 모두 말없이 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: After the ceremony ended, everyone went home in silence.

explain: 돌아가신 사람을 기억하려고 여는 행사예요. '장례식'은 돌아가신 직후에 치르는 의식이고, 추모식은 시간이 지난 뒤나 기념일에 여는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is an event held to remember someone who has passed away. 장례식 is the funeral right after the death, whereas a 추모식 is often held later or on an anniversary.

examples.en: There are many small gears inside a watch.
I observed the gears turning as they meshed.
I oiled the bicycle's gear.

examples.ko: 톱니바퀴 하나가 고장 나면 전체가 멈춰요.
examples.en: If one gear breaks, the whole thing stops.
I'm a part of the big cogwheel called the company.
The child eagerly assembled a gear toy.

explain: 기계 부품을 말하지만 큰 조직 안에서 맡은 일만 반복하는 사람을 비유할 때도 자주 써요. 외래어 '기어'는 자동차나 자전거의 속도 조절 장치를 말할 때 더 흔해요.

phrases.example: 두 부서의 일이 톱니바퀴처럼 맞물려 돌아가요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이나 일이 빈틈없이 이어져 잘 돌아간다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people or tasks fitting together smoothly with no gaps.

explain_en: It names a machine part, but is also used figuratively for a person who just repeats their role inside a big organization. The loanword 기어 is more common for the speed gears of cars and bikes.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 밥 먹을 때 틀니를 끼세요.
examples.en: Grandpa puts in his dentures when he eats.

examples.ko: 틀니가 잘 맞지 않아서 치과에 갔어요.
examples.en: The dentures didn't fit well, so I went to the dentist.
My father got new dentures last year.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 틀니를 깨끗이 닦아야 해요.
examples.en: You have to clean your dentures before going to bed.
Because of the dentures, avoid hard food.
When you get dentures, speaking is awkward at first.

explain: 의학 용어로는 '의치'라고 하지만 일상에서는 '틀니'라고 해요. 몇 개만 끼우는 건 '부분 틀니', 전체는 '완전 틀니'라고 해요. 어르신에게는 '틀니를 하시다'처럼 높여요.
explain_en: The medical term is 의치, but in daily life people say 틀니. A partial set is 부분 틀니 and a full set is 완전 틀니. For elders you raise it: '틀니를 하시다'.

examples.en: Whales live by eating plankton.
There is a lot of plankton in seawater.

examples.ko: 플랑크톤은 너무 작아서 눈에 안 보여요.
examples.en: Plankton is so small that you can't see it.

examples.ko: 플랑크톤이 갑자기 늘면 물 색이 변하기도 해요.
examples.en: If plankton suddenly increases, the water's color can change.
In science class we looked at plankton under a microscope.
Small fish grow up eating plankton.

explain: 식물처럼 광합성을 하는 것은 '식물 플랑크톤', 움직이며 먹이를 먹는 것은 '동물 플랑크톤'이라고 해요. 과학 시간이나 바다, 환경 뉴스에 주로 나와요.
explain_en: The photosynthesizing kind is 식물 플랑크톤, and the kind that moves and feeds is 동물 플랑크톤. It mostly appears in science class and in news about the sea or the environment.

examples.en: The drain is clogged, so the water won't go down.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 하수구에서 물이 넘쳐요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, water overflows from the drain.
Hair often gets stuck in the drain.
A sewer smell came up, so I opened the window.
I dropped my key down the drain.
Drains need to be cleaned regularly.

explain: 원래 길 아래 큰 물길은 '하수구', 집 안 욕실이나 싱크대의 구멍은 '배수구'라고 구별해요. 하지만 일상에서는 집 안의 구멍도 '하수구'라고 하는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: Strictly, the large channel under the street is 하수구 and the hole in a bathroom or sink is 배수구. In daily life, though, many people call the one at home 하수구 as well.

examples.en: Books are piled up in a corner of the room.
A part of my heart kept feeling uneasy.
The child was crying quietly in a corner.
I tossed my bag into a corner.
I found a small doll in a corner of the shop.
If you leave a corner empty, it's convenient later.

explain: '구석'은 모서리 안쪽 장소이고, '한구석'은 '어느 한 구석'이라는 느낌이 강해서 '방 한구석', '마음 한구석'처럼 써요. 마음속에 작게 남은 감정을 말할 때 특히 자주 나와요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 크지는 않지만 마음속 어딘가에 남은 감정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a feeling that is small but lingers somewhere inside.
phrases.en_equiv: in the back of one's mind

explain_en: 구석 is the inner part of a corner, while 한구석 has the feel of 'one corner somewhere', as in '방 한구석' and '마음 한구석'. It is especially common for a small feeling lingering in the heart.

examples.en: We found a caregiver to look after my mother.
A caregiver helps the patient eat, staying by their side.
The caregiver watched over the patient all night at the hospital.
The cost of a caregiver is higher than I expected.

examples.ko: 가족 대신 간병인이 환자를 씻겨 줘요.
examples.en: Instead of family, a caregiver bathes the patient.
I passed on my thanks to the caregiver.

explain: 병원이나 집에서 환자 옆에서 먹고 씻는 일을 도와주는 사람이에요. 치료는 하지 않아서 의사나 간호사와 달라요. '간호사'와 헷갈리지 않게 주의하세요.
explain_en: This is a person who stays with a patient at a hospital or home and helps with eating and washing. They do not give medical treatment, unlike doctors or nurses, so don't confuse 간병인 with 간호사.

examples.en: That comedian's facial expressions are really funny.
When I was little, my dream was to be a comedian.
The comedian sang a song on the broadcast.

examples.ko: 저는 개그우먼 한 분을 아주 좋아해요.
examples.en: I really like one of the comedians.
I took a photo with my comedian friend.
People lined up to see the comedian.

explain: 남자는 '개그맨', 여자는 '개그우먼'이라고 해요. 성별 없이 부를 때는 '코미디언'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: A male one is a 개그맨 and a female one is a 개그우먼. To refer to either without gender, people also say 코미디언.

examples.en: My clothes got soaked in the sudden rain.
The news was so sudden that I was shocked.
The appointment was suddenly canceled.
It was hard to adapt to the abrupt change.

examples.ko: 할아버지의 급작스러운 입원에 가족이 모두 모였어요.
examples.en: The whole family gathered after Grandpa's sudden hospitalization.
It was sudden, but we handled it well.

explain: '갑작스럽다'와 거의 같게 쓰는데, 말할 때는 '갑작스럽다'가 훨씬 흔해요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '급작스러워요', '급작스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 주로 '급작스러운 변화'처럼 명사 앞에서 써요.
explain_en: Used almost like 갑작스럽다, which is much more common in speech. It is a ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes 급작스러워요 and 급작스러운. It mostly appears before a noun, as in '급작스러운 변화'.

examples.en: I decided to become an organ donor.
We kept the donor's name secret.
Thanks to the donor, the patient regained health.
The library sent a thank-you letter to the donor.
The donor brought this book in person.

examples.ko: 기증자는 먼저 건강 검사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: A donor has to take a health check first.

explain: '기증하다'는 대가 없이 주는 것이고 기증자는 그 사람이에요. 피를 주는 사람은 '헌혈자', 돈을 내는 사람은 '기부자'라고 해서 쓰임이 달라요. 장기, 책, 작품 같은 걸 줄 때 '기증자'를 써요.
explain_en: 기증하다 means giving without payment, and the 기증자 is that giver. A blood donor is a 헌혈자 and a money donor is a 기부자, so the usage differs. 기증자 is used for organs, books, artworks and similar gifts.

en: show off; act pushy; butt in

examples.en: Why are you showing off so much?

examples.ko: 아무도 안 시켰는데 혼자 나대고 있어요.
examples.en: Nobody told him to, but he's busy butting in alone.
If you make a fuss over nothing, it's actually embarrassing.
My friend was showing off, and the mood got weird.
That kid tends to show off everywhere.
Don't push yourself forward so much, and stay quiet.

explain: 필요 없이 나서거나 잘난 척하며 설치는 사람에게 쓰는 부정적인 말투예요. 친구끼리 농담으로 쓰기도 하지만 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게 쓰면 무례해요. 비슷한 말로 '설치다', '깝죽대다'가 있어요.
explain_en: A negative word for someone who pushes themselves forward or acts smug when it isn't needed. Friends may use it as a joke, but it is rude to elders or people you've just met. Similar words are 설치다 and 깝죽대다.

examples.en: I have astigmatism, so I wear glasses.
The letters look blurry because of astigmatism.
You can get astigmatism checked at an eye clinic.

examples.ko: 동생은 난시가 심해서 밤 운전을 못 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has severe astigmatism and can't drive at night.
I got new lenses for astigmatism.
At my eye test I was told I have astigmatism.

explain: 눈 이야기에서 '근시'는 먼 곳이 흐리게 보이는 것, '원시'는 가까운 곳이 흐리게 보이는 것이고 난시는 물체가 겹치거나 번져 보이는 거예요. 안경 처방에서 '난시가 있다'고 해요.
explain_en: Among eye conditions, 근시 blurs far objects and 원시 blurs near ones, while 난시 makes things look doubled or smeared. In a prescription you say '난시가 있다'.
